public_rationale: The records establish substantial losses at Anthropic and MiniMax and major external financing at Anthropic. They do not establish that the entire industry has unsustainable economics. Midjourney provides relevant counterevidence to the universal wording, but its cited account lacks comparable 2025 financials. The unspecified accounting basis also prevents a supported or contradicted financial verdict under the assessment rules.
limitations: Individual companies cannot establish an industry-wide financial conclusion.
Present losses are not proof of permanent unsustainability.
The strongest counterexample is qualitative and outside the selected reporting period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The generative AI industry runs on unprofitable, unsustainable economics funded by speculation.

statement.excerpt: The entire generative AI industry is based on unprofitable, unsustainable economics, rationalized and funded by venture capitalists and bankers speculating on the theoretical value of Large Language Model-based services.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: funded by venture capitalists and bankers
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that generative AI businesses depend on outside financing because their services cannot durably cover their full costs.
I use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual financial period before publication, consistent with the surrounding discussion of 2025 results.
Current losses, dependence on financing, and lasting economic unsustainability are distinct propositions. Evidence of the first two does not establish the third.
The industry-wide assertion requires evidence beyond selected loss-making companies. The words do not specify an accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Representative financial and operating records establish industry-wide losses, dependence on speculative outside financing, and an inability to sustain operations through customer receipts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish durable, independently financed profitability in a material part of the industry; a verified sustainable counterexample would also challenge the literal assertion about the entire industry.

evidence.locator: Risk Factors, page 64; financial-statement audit opinion, page F-3
evidence.publisher: Anthropic, PBC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence.explanation: The filing reports a 2025 net loss of $42.0 billion, including $34.3 billion of financial-instrument fair-value changes. This establishes losses at Anthropic, not equivalent cash consumption or industry-wide permanent unsustainability.

evidence.publisher: MiniMax Group Inc., distributed by PR Newswire
evidence.explanation: MiniMax reported substantial adjusted losses. The measure excludes share-based compensation, financial-liability fair-value losses, and listing expenses; it does not establish the economics of the whole industry.
This confirms major outside financing during the target period. Raising capital does not itself establish that services are unsustainable or that investors lack an economic rationale.

evidence.locator: Entrepreneurship discussion following Holz's account of founding Leap Motion
evidence.explanation: The organizer's account of Holz's May appearance describes a profitable, independently funded generative AI company. This challenges the universal wording, but supplies neither a 2025 profit figure nor an accounting basis.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable financial and financing records across a defined industry population, with an explicit accounting basis and evidence about durable full-cost profitability.
